title: "Audit 7: evidence for the functional gene groups used in the contrasts"
author: "Jannik Franken"

## Purpose

Two contrasts combine genes into one group. The NRF2 positive control counts a
lung line as altered when KEAP1 **or** NFE2L2 is altered (`pathway_groups` in
`config.yml`). The MTAP deletion contrast reads MTAP loss as loss of the 9p21
locus, because MTAP is almost always deleted together with CDKN2A. A grouping
like this needs evidence that the genes act in the same way. This notebook
collects that evidence from three sources:

1. published work (verified bibliographic records),
2. prior knowledge in OmniPath Metabo: direct functional interactions and
   shared pathways in KEGG, Reactome and WikiPathways,
3. data: mutual exclusivity (NRF2) or co-deletion (9p21) across all DepMap
   models.

**Decision supported:** whether the NRF2 group (KEAP1 + NFE2L2) and the 9p21
reading of the MTAP contrast can be used as specified at Checkpoint 2.

## Inputs

- OmniPath Metabo database, default deployment of `metabo.figures` (dev5), read only
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/depmap_24Q4/`: `Model.csv`, `OmicsSomaticMutations.csv`, `OmicsAbsoluteCNGene.csv` (DepMap 24Q4, local only)
- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds` (lines used in models)
- `config.yml`: `contrast` (gene roles, groups), `depmap`

## Methods

Interactions and pathways were read from the OmniPath Metabo Postgres
database. Genes were matched to database entities by gene symbol, Entrez ID
and UniProt accession, taking the identifiers from DepMap so that no
non-human ortholog is included. Direct interactions are relations between the
group members in any resource; sign and direction come from the per-resource
interaction facts. Pathway membership is any relation between a gene and an
entity of type "pathway" in KEGG, Reactome or WikiPathways.

For the data check, a DepMap model counts as altered with the same definition
as in the contrasts: oncogenes (NFE2L2) need a likely-driver variant; tumour
suppressors (KEAP1) count with any protein-changing variant or a homozygous
deletion (absolute copy number 0). Only models with both mutation calls and
copy number were used. Mutual exclusivity was tested with Fisher's exact test
(all models and lung), and with the Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test stratified
by lineage, which removes the confounding by tissue. An odds ratio below 1
means the two alterations occur together less often than expected.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# metabo.figures provides the database connection and query provenance
# (loaded first, so that the use-case helpers below take precedence)
pkgload::load_all(here::here(), export_all = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
config <- load_config()
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
fig_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_07_functional_groups")

# DepMap files of the release given in config.yml
depmap_dir <- file.path(raw_dir, config$depmap$dir)
depmap_files <- c(
    models = file.path(depmap_dir, "Model.csv"),
    mutations = file.path(depmap_dir, "OmicsSomaticMutations.csv"),
    copy_number = file.path(depmap_dir, "OmicsAbsoluteCNGene.csv")
)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(depmap_files)))

# the groups examined here
nrf2_genes <- config$contrast$pathway_groups$NRF2
locus_9p21 <- c("MTAP", "CDKN2A")
all_genes <- c(nrf2_genes, locus_9p21)
```

## 1. Literature

Verified against Europe PMC (title, authors, journal, DOI) on 2026-10-29.

## 2. Prior knowledge in OmniPath Metabo

### Database and gene entities

```{r db-connect}
con <- pg_connect()
db_build <- build_manifest_for(con)
c(build_id = db_build$build_id, built_at = db_build$built_at)

# human identifiers of the genes, taken from DepMap (symbol, Entrez ID, UniProt)
gene_ids <- data.table::fread(depmap_files[["mutations"]],
                              select = c("HugoSymbol", "EntrezGeneID", "UniprotID")) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    filter(HugoSymbol %in% all_genes) %>%
    # DepMap gives UniProt isoforms ("Q16236-1"); the database uses the accession
    distinct(gene = HugoSymbol, entrez = as.character(EntrezGeneID),
             uniprot = na_if(sub("-[0-9]+$", "", UniprotID), "")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(entrez))
gene_ids

# protein entities in the database carrying one of these identifiers
identifiers <- unique(na.omit(c(gene_ids$gene, gene_ids$entrez, gene_ids$uniprot)))
quoted <- paste(DBI::dbQuoteString(con, identifiers), collapse = ", ")
entities <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT e.entity_id::text AS entity_id, e.canonical_identifier, e.label
    FROM omnipath.entity e
    JOIN omnipath.vocab_entity_type t ON t.entity_type_id = e.entity_type_id
    WHERE t.name = 'protein' AND e.canonical_identifier IN (%s)", quoted))

# each entity belongs to the gene whose symbol, Entrez ID or UniProt it carries
id_to_gene <- bind_rows(
    transmute(gene_ids, canonical_identifier = gene, gene),
    transmute(gene_ids, canonical_identifier = entrez, gene),
    transmute(gene_ids, canonical_identifier = uniprot, gene)
) %>%
    distinct()
entities <- entities %>% inner_join(id_to_gene, by = "canonical_identifier")
preview_table(entities, caption = "Database entities of the genes")
entity_list <- paste(DBI::dbQuoteString(con, entities$entity_id), collapse = ", ")
```

### Direct interactions between KEAP1 and NFE2L2

```{r interactions}
# relations between two of the genes, any resource
relations <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT ds.name AS resource, cat.name AS category, p.name AS predicate,
           re.subject_entity_id::text AS subject_id, re.object_entity_id::text AS object_id
    FROM omnipath.relation_evidence re
    JOIN omnipath.data_source ds ON ds.source_id = re.source_id
    JOIN omnipath.vocab_relation_category cat ON cat.relation_category_id = re.relation_category_id
    JOIN omnipath.vocab_relation_predicate p ON p.relation_predicate_id = re.predicate_id
    WHERE re.subject_entity_id::text IN (%1$s) AND re.object_entity_id::text IN (%1$s)", entity_list))

# direction, sign and references per resource from the interaction facts
facts <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT ds.name AS resource,
           f.subject_entity_id::text AS subject_id, f.object_entity_id::text AS object_id,
           f.is_directed, f.is_stimulation, f.is_inhibition,
           array_to_string(f.reference_pubmed_ids, ';') AS pmids
    FROM omnipath.interaction_fact_resource f
    JOIN omnipath.data_source ds ON ds.source_id = f.source_id
    WHERE f.subject_entity_id::text IN (%1$s) AND f.object_entity_id::text IN (%1$s)", entity_list))

gene_of <- setNames(entities$gene, entities$entity_id)
nrf2_pair <- function(x) {
    x %>%
        mutate(subject = gene_of[subject_id], object = gene_of[object_id]) %>%
        filter(subject %in% nrf2_genes, object %in% nrf2_genes, subject != object)
}

# one row per resource and direction
interaction_summary <- nrf2_pair(facts) %>%
    group_by(resource, direction = paste(subject, "->", object)) %>%
    summarise(
        directed = any(is_directed %in% TRUE),
        inhibition = any(is_inhibition %in% TRUE),
        stimulation = any(is_stimulation %in% TRUE),
        n_pubmed = n_distinct(unlist(strsplit(na.omit(pmids), ";"))),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    full_join(
        nrf2_pair(relations) %>%
            group_by(resource, direction = paste(subject, "->", object)) %>%
            summarise(predicates = paste(sort(unique(predicate)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop"),
        by = c("resource", "direction")
    ) %>%
    mutate(evidence = case_when(
        directed & inhibition ~ "directed, inhibition",
        directed & stimulation ~ "directed, stimulation",
        directed ~ "directed, no sign",
        TRUE ~ "undirected (binding)"
    )) %>%
    arrange(evidence, resource)
preview_table(interaction_summary, caption = "KEAP1-NFE2L2 interactions per resource")

c(resources = n_distinct(interaction_summary$resource),
  resources_KEAP1_inhibits_NFE2L2 = n_distinct(interaction_summary$resource[
      interaction_summary$direction == "KEAP1 -> NFE2L2" & interaction_summary$inhibition %in% TRUE]),
  resources_stimulation = sum(interaction_summary$stimulation %in% TRUE))
```

```{r interactions-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
p <- interaction_summary %>%
    mutate(resource = forcats::fct_rev(factor(resource))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(direction, resource, fill = evidence)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(c("directed, inhibition", "directed, stimulation",
                                            "directed, no sign", "undirected (binding)"))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = "KEAP1-NFE2L2 interactions in OmniPath Metabo",
         subtitle = paste("build", db_build$build_id)) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "keap1_nfe2l2_interactions", fig_dir)
p
```

### Shared pathways in KEGG, Reactome and WikiPathways

```{r pathways}
# gene-pathway relations in the three pathway resources (either direction)
pathway_relations <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT DISTINCT ds.name AS resource, cat.name AS category,
           g.entity_id::text AS gene_entity, pw.canonical_identifier AS pathway_id, pw.label AS pathway
    FROM omnipath.relation_evidence re
    JOIN omnipath.data_source ds ON ds.source_id = re.source_id
    JOIN omnipath.vocab_relation_category cat ON cat.relation_category_id = re.relation_category_id
    JOIN omnipath.entity g ON g.entity_id IN (re.subject_entity_id, re.object_entity_id)
    JOIN omnipath.entity pw ON pw.entity_id IN (re.subject_entity_id, re.object_entity_id)
    JOIN omnipath.vocab_entity_type t ON t.entity_type_id = pw.entity_type_id
    WHERE ds.name IN ('kegg', 'reactome', 'wikipathways')
      AND t.name = 'pathway'
      AND (re.subject_entity_id::text IN (%1$s) OR re.object_entity_id::text IN (%1$s))
      AND g.entity_id::text IN (%1$s)", entity_list)) %>%
    mutate(gene = gene_of[gene_entity]) %>%
    distinct(resource, category, gene, pathway_id, pathway)

# pathways per resource containing KEAP1, NFE2L2 or both
nrf2_pathways <- pathway_relations %>%
    filter(gene %in% nrf2_genes) %>%
    group_by(resource, pathway_id, pathway) %>%
    summarise(genes = paste(sort(unique(gene)), collapse = " + "), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(membership = if_else(genes == paste(sort(nrf2_genes), collapse = " + "), "both", paste(genes, "only")))
nrf2_pathways %>% count(resource, membership) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = membership, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

nrf2_pathways %>%
    filter(membership == "both") %>%
    arrange(resource, pathway) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Pathways containing both KEAP1 and NFE2L2")
```

```{r pathways-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
p <- nrf2_pathways %>%
    count(resource, membership) %>%
    ggplot(aes(resource, n, fill = membership)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(c("both", "KEAP1 only", "NFE2L2 only"))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Pathways", fill = NULL,
         title = "Pathways containing KEAP1 and/or NFE2L2 (OmniPath Metabo)") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "nrf2_pathways", fig_dir)
p
```

The same query for MTAP and CDKN2A shows whether pathways relate them; their
grouping rests on genomic position, not on function, so shared pathways are
not expected.

```{r pathways-9p21}
pathway_relations %>%
    filter(gene %in% locus_9p21) %>%
    group_by(resource, pathway_id, pathway) %>%
    summarise(genes = paste(sort(unique(gene)), collapse = " + "), .groups = "drop") %>%
    count(resource, genes)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## 3. Data: DepMap models

```{r depmap}
# DepMap models with lineage
models <- readr::read_csv(depmap_files[["models"]], col_select = c(ModelID, OncotreeLineage),
                          show_col_types = FALSE)

# protein-changing variants of the four genes, with DepMap's driver flags (as in step 04)
flag_columns <- c("Hotspot", "LikelyLoF", "HessDriver", "OncogeneHighImpact", "TumorSuppressorHighImpact")
variants <- data.table::fread(depmap_files[["mutations"]],
                              select = c("ModelID", "HugoSymbol", "ProteinChange", flag_columns)) %>%
    as_tibble()
mutated_models <- unique(variants$ModelID)
# protein-changing variants per model, used below to recognise hypermutated models
variants_per_model <- count(variants, ModelID, name = "n_variants")
variants <- variants %>%
    filter(HugoSymbol %in% all_genes) %>%
    group_by(ModelID, gene = HugoSymbol) %>%
    summarise(any_mutation = TRUE,
              protein_changes = paste(unique(na.omit(ProteinChange)), collapse = "; "),
              likely_driver = any(Hotspot | LikelyLoF | HessDriver | OncogeneHighImpact | TumorSuppressorHighImpact),
              .groups = "drop")

# absolute copy number of the four genes; 0 = homozygous deletion
cn_header <- names(data.table::fread(depmap_files[["copy_number"]], nrows = 0))
cn_columns <- cn_header[sub(" \\(.*$", "", cn_header) %in% all_genes]
cn <- data.table::fread(depmap_files[["copy_number"]], select = c(cn_header[1], cn_columns)) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    rename(ModelID = 1) %>%
    pivot_longer(-ModelID, names_to = "gene", values_to = "copy_number") %>%
    mutate(gene = sub(" \\(.*$", "", gene))

# models with both mutation calls and copy number
universe <- models %>% filter(ModelID %in% mutated_models, ModelID %in% cn$ModelID)
c(models = nrow(models), with_mutations = length(mutated_models), with_both = nrow(universe))

# status per model and gene, with the definition of "altered" by gene role (decision Q1)
status <- tidyr::expand_grid(ModelID = universe$ModelID, gene = all_genes) %>%
    left_join(variants, by = c("ModelID", "gene")) %>%
    left_join(cn, by = c("ModelID", "gene")) %>%
    mutate(
        any_mutation = coalesce(any_mutation, FALSE),
        likely_driver = coalesce(likely_driver, FALSE),
        deleted = coalesce(copy_number == 0, FALSE),
        altered = if_else(gene %in% config$contrast$oncogenes, likely_driver, any_mutation | deleted)
    ) %>%
    left_join(universe, by = "ModelID")
status %>% group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(altered = sum(altered), mutated = sum(any_mutation), deleted = sum(deleted))
```

### NRF2: mutual exclusivity of KEAP1 and NFE2L2

```{r exclusivity}
nrf2_status <- status %>%
    filter(gene %in% nrf2_genes) %>%
    select(ModelID, OncotreeLineage, gene, altered) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = gene, values_from = altered)

# 2x2 table over all models, and Fisher's exact test
table(KEAP1 = nrf2_status$KEAP1, NFE2L2 = nrf2_status$NFE2L2)
fisher_all <- fisher.test(table(nrf2_status$KEAP1, nrf2_status$NFE2L2))

# lung only
lung <- filter(nrf2_status, OncotreeLineage == "Lung")
table(KEAP1 = lung$KEAP1, NFE2L2 = lung$NFE2L2)
fisher_lung <- fisher.test(table(lung$KEAP1, lung$NFE2L2))

# stratified by lineage; strata need both genes altered at least once somewhere to inform the test
informative <- nrf2_status %>%
    group_by(OncotreeLineage) %>%
    filter(n() >= 2, any(KEAP1), any(NFE2L2)) %>%
    ungroup()
cmh <- mantelhaen.test(table(informative$KEAP1, informative$NFE2L2, informative$OncotreeLineage), exact = TRUE)

tibble(
    test = c("Fisher, all models", "Fisher, lung", "CMH, by lineage"),
    models = c(nrow(nrf2_status), nrow(lung), nrow(informative)),
    odds_ratio = c(fisher_all$estimate, fisher_lung$estimate, cmh$estimate),
    p_value = c(fisher_all$p.value, fisher_lung$p.value, cmh$p.value)
)
```

```{r exclusivity-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# altered models per lineage, split by which gene is altered
p <- nrf2_status %>%
    filter(KEAP1 | NFE2L2) %>%
    mutate(alteration = case_when(KEAP1 & NFE2L2 ~ "both", KEAP1 ~ "KEAP1 only", TRUE ~ "NFE2L2 only")) %>%
    count(OncotreeLineage, alteration) %>%
    group_by(OncotreeLineage) %>% filter(sum(n) >= 3) %>% ungroup() %>%
    ggplot(aes(n, forcats::fct_reorder(OncotreeLineage, n, sum), fill = alteration)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(c("both", "KEAP1 only", "NFE2L2 only"))) +
    labs(x = "DepMap models", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = "KEAP1 and NFE2L2 alterations across DepMap lineages",
         subtitle = "lineages with at least 3 altered models") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "nrf2_exclusivity", fig_dir)
p
```

Models with both genes altered, with their number of protein-changing
variants and its percentile among all models. Many co-occurrences in highly
mutated models would point to passenger variants rather than to two
independent hits in the pathway.

```{r co-altered}
burden <- variants_per_model %>%
    filter(ModelID %in% universe$ModelID) %>%
    mutate(burden_percentile = round(100 * percent_rank(n_variants)))
nrf2_status %>%
    filter(KEAP1, NFE2L2) %>%
    left_join(burden, by = "ModelID") %>%
    left_join(
        status %>%
            filter(gene %in% nrf2_genes) %>%
            select(ModelID, gene, protein_changes, likely_driver, deleted) %>%
            pivot_wider(names_from = gene, values_from = c(protein_changes, likely_driver, deleted)),
        by = "ModelID"
    ) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "DepMap models with KEAP1 and NFE2L2 altered")
```

The lung lines of the Shorthouse data set, with the same definition:

```{r exclusivity-shorthouse}
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/mutations.R"))
analysis_data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
lung_lines <- analysis_data$lines %>% filter(in_models, tissue == "Lung") %>% pull(line)
alteration_status(analysis_data, lung_lines, nrf2_genes) %>%
    mutate(altered = if_else(gene %in% config$contrast$oncogenes, likely_driver, any_mutation | deleted)) %>%
    select(line, gene, altered) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = gene, values_from = altered) %>%
    count(KEAP1, NFE2L2)
```

### 9p21: co-deletion of MTAP and CDKN2A

```{r codeletion}
deletion_status <- status %>%
    filter(gene %in% locus_9p21) %>%
    select(ModelID, OncotreeLineage, gene, deleted) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = gene, values_from = deleted)
table(MTAP = deletion_status$MTAP, CDKN2A = deletion_status$CDKN2A)
fisher.test(table(deletion_status$MTAP, deletion_status$CDKN2A))
c(MTAP_deleted = sum(deletion_status$MTAP),
  with_CDKN2A = sum(deletion_status$MTAP & deletion_status$CDKN2A),
  share = mean(deletion_status$CDKN2A[deletion_status$MTAP]))
```

## Interpretation

**NRF2 group (KEAP1 + NFE2L2): supported by literature and prior knowledge,
not by mutual exclusivity.**

- *Literature:* both genes form the curated NRF2 pathway of Sanchez-Vega et
  al. (2018), where alterations of the members are analysed together.
- *Interactions (OmniPath Metabo):* 20 resources link KEAP1 and NFE2L2. Six
  of them (SIGNOR, NRF2ome, SPIKE, WikiPathways, Laudanna, Wang) give a
  directed, inhibitory KEAP1 → NFE2L2 edge, and no resource gives a
  stimulatory one. The remaining resources report binding (BioGRID, IntAct,
  HIPPIE and others, together > 100 PubMed IDs). A loss of KEAP1 and a gain
  of NFE2L2 therefore act in the same direction: both release NFE2L2.
- *Pathways (OmniPath Metabo):* the two genes share pathways in all three
  resources (KEGG 5, Reactome 5, WikiPathways 3), including the specific
  Reactome "KEAP1-NFE2L2 pathway" (R-HSA-9755511) and "Nuclear events
  mediated by NFE2L2", and KEGG "Chemical carcinogenesis – reactive oxygen
  species". Some shared entries are broad (Reactome "Cellular responses to
  stimuli", KEGG "Pathways in cancer") and add little on their own.
- *Data (DepMap):* mutual exclusivity is **not** shown. Across all 1607
  models the two co-occur more often than expected (odds ratio 4.0); within
  lineages (CMH) and in lung the tests are not significant. In lung, none of
  the 41 altered models carries both alterations, but with 5 NFE2L2-altered
  models this is uninformative. Four of the five co-altered models are
  uterine and lie at the 98th–99th percentile of mutation burden, and in four of
  the five KEAP1 is altered only through a variant DepMap does not flag as a
  likely driver. The co-occurrence across all models thus reflects passenger
  variants in hypermutated models, not two hits in the same pathway.
- *Shorthouse lung lines:* 19 KEAP1-altered, 5 NFE2L2-altered, none both, so
  the group in the positive control combines two disjoint sets of lines.

**Caveat raised by this audit:** the definition "any protein-changing variant
or homozygous deletion" for tumour suppressors (decision Q1) counts passenger
variants in hypermutated lines. This matters little in lung, but it affects
pan-tissue contrasts (KRAS covariates, screen) wherever hypermutated lines
(e.g. uterus, colon) contribute.

**9p21 (MTAP with CDKN2A): supported.** Three verified references attribute
MTAP loss to its proximity to CDKN2A. In DepMap, 264 of 273 MTAP-deleted models
(97 %) also have CDKN2A deleted (odds ratio 179). As expected for a positional
grouping, no pathway in the three resources contains both genes. An effect of
the MTAP contrast cannot be attributed to MTAP alone and is read as 9p21 loss.

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```
